target: Six independent build jobs start together. By the observation cutoff, one completed at time 2; one still-running job was withdrawn from observation at time 3; two completed at time 4; and two still-running jobs were censored at time 5. The team must estimate the probability a comparable job remains unfinished past time 4 while handling the censored jobs correctly, rather than averaging only completed durations.
surface: A previous build dashboard discarded still-running jobs and averaged the three completed durations 2, 4, and 4 to report 3.33 time units. It did not adjust the risk set when jobs were censored.
structural: A clinical time-to-event study used the Kaplan-Meier product-limit estimator under right censoring. At each event time j it multiplied survival by (n_j-d_j)/n_j, where n_j was the risk set immediately before the event and d_j the number of events; censorings reduced later risk sets but did not create survival drops.
rubric: Explicitly selects the Kaplan-Meier product-limit estimator for right-censored completion times.
At time 2 uses risk set 6 and one completion, giving factor 5/6; after the time-3 censoring uses risk set 4 before time 4.
At time 4 uses two completions and factor (4-2)/4=1/2.
Computes S(4)=(5/6)*(1/2)=5/12, about 0.417 unfinished past time 4.
States independent/non-informative censoring and comparable-job assumptions.
